items.heading: Sequence Matters More Than Speed
items.text: Sequence matters more than speed. Financial triage first, decision second, applications third, networking running underneath all of it.

items.heading: If You Are Searching
items.text: If you are searching for this right now, you are reacting to a real and well-documented pattern, not a personal streak of bad luck.

items.heading: Before You Rewrite a Single
items.text: Before you rewrite a single resume bullet, get a clear, factual picture of your money situation. This single step does more to calm panic than any pep talk, because it replaces a vague fear with an actual number.

columns: Why it comes before the job
rows: Add up cash, liquid mutual funds, and fixed deposits. Divide by your true monthly non-negotiable spend (EMIs, rent, food, insurance, school fees). That number of months is your runway, not a guess, a fact you can plan around.
Full and final settlement, gratuity if you cross the eligibility period, leave encashment, and any pending bonus or variable pay. This is money already earned, not a favour from your former employer.
Pause, do not panic-stop, your investments

A SIP running on zero income is not discipline, it is a hole in your runway. Pause it, keep the mandate active, and restart once income resumes, do not redeem long-term investments unless the runway math forces it.
Talk to lenders before you miss a payment
Banks and NBFCs increasingly offer moratoriums or restructuring for a genuine job loss. A call before a missed EMI protects your credit score; a call after does not undo the damage as easily.

items.heading: 01 Was Your Role Automatable,
items.text: 01 Was your role automatable, or was it your specific employer's cost-cutting? These need very different fixes. If AI copilots or process automation genuinely absorbed the routine part of your job, the fix is a skill layer, not just a new employer doing the same work. If it was pure cost-cutting in a healthy function, your existing skill set may still be sellable as-is.

items.heading: 02 Which Layer of Your
items.text: 02 Which layer of your work still needed a human, and which did not? List your last year of tasks honestly. Mark each one: judgment-heavy or execution-only. Roles that were mostly execution-only are the ones companies are actively compressing right now, across levels, not just entry-level.

items.heading: 03 What Did You Avoid
items.text: 03 What did you avoid learning because the old job never forced it? Most professionals can name one skill gap honestly within a minute of being asked directly. That gap, not a generic "upskilling" list, is usually the one worth closing first.
